behaviours.excerpt: Manufacturers must report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury/property-damage event involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours
behaviours.comparison: Scope is limited to listed events, so minor overheating and smoke events without damage are excluded, and customer notice for non-material incidents has no fixed deadline ('next scheduled safety communication'). Both are weaker than the S1 acceptable range in a section both companies benefit from weakening.

fact_claims.verbatim: Ember 8 had a 3.9% failure rate at 55 °C
9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
four incidents were not reported to a regulator

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury/property-damage event involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a complete incident report within 10 calendar days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk or requires customer action; otherwise, include it in the next scheduled safety communication.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% triggers prompt regulator notification, investigation, and a corrective-action and retest plan. Regulators may allow time-limited conditional certification or continued sales under monitoring and appropriate safeguards while remediation is underway; they determine measures for installed units. Individual-company per-model failure rates are not required to be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with protections against unauthorized access and clear customer instructions. For units already installed when the requirement takes effect, manufacturers must provide remote shut-off through retrofit or an equivalent safe upgrade within 6 years, where technically feasible. Customers must receive advance notice and instructions; emergency procedures must not depend solely on remote connectivity.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of thermal propagation. Manufacturers must document performance using a regulator-approved test protocol and provide results to the relevant regulator and customers.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A notice requiring immediate action must be sent within 72 hours of determining that action is needed; other material safety information must be included in the next scheduled safety communication. Manufacturers must notify the relevant regulator and affected customers when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. Exceeding that threshold triggers a mandatory recall

document.section_notes: The final text makes the 5% S2 limit a trigger for notification and remediation rather than a sales stop, and lets regulators allow continued sales, while keeping per-model results to purchasers and regulators and out of public view. S3 sets new-unit shut-off at 24 months and retrofit at 6 years, and S4 sets built-in suppression at 36 months, which sits inside the acceptable range. S5 keeps a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, though it adds that recall does not by itself mean permanent exclusion, which leaves regulators room to set remedies and conditional certification.
